features.name: Buy Again
features.description: A one-tap action on any past order that loads its full contents into the cart for editing.
features.hmw: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual order without hunting down each item?

features.name: My Regulars list
features.description: A standing list of the shopper's core items they can tick into the cart in one screen instead of searching each week.
features.hmw: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual order without hunting down each item?

features.name: Per-item substitution rules
features.description: Set once per product or category whether to allow a swap, choose from a shortlist, or refund if it's out of stock.
features.hmw: How might we keep shoppers in control when something they wanted turns out to be unavailable?

features.name: Approve-the-swap notification
features.description: When an item goes out of stock at pick time, notify the shopper with a proposed alternative to accept or reject before dispatch.
features.hmw: How might we keep shoppers in control when something they wanted turns out to be unavailable?

features.name: Never-substitute default
features.description: An account-level setting that removes any item that can't be fulfilled rather than swapping it, no per-item setup.
features.hmw: How might we keep shoppers in control when something they wanted turns out to be unavailable?

features.name: AM/PM delivery windows
features.description: Let shoppers pick a morning or afternoon slot at checkout instead of a whole day, narrowing to a 2-hour window on the day.
features.hmw: How might we make a delivery's timing predictable enough to plan a household around?

features.name: Proactive delay alerts
features.description: When an order will miss its slot, push a message with the reason and a new ETA rather than leaving the shopper to guess.

features.name: Per-order impact receipt
features.description: Replace the bare score with a plain-language summary of what this order did: local farms supported, produce-waste prevented, average food miles.

features.name: Your GreenBasket story

features.name: Seasonal picks module
features.description: A curated 'what's good and new this week' section on the home screen that changes with the season and stock.

features.name: Producer stories in browse

design_directions.name: Two Taps to Done
design_directions.summary: Bet that GreenBasket wins by being the fastest way to run a known weekly shop. Rebuild the home screen around the repeat order and remove every surprise; discovery is a secondary surface.
design_directions.differentiator: A reorder-first home built on your regulars and last order, substitution rules set once, and delivery windows tight enough to plan around — the whole shop in under two minutes.
hmws_addressed: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual order without hunting down each item?
How might we keep shoppers in control when something they wanted turns out to be unavailable?
How might we make a delivery's timing predictable enough to plan a household around?
design_directions.tradeoff: Gives up the market-discovery feeling the values-driven shopper wants; risks reading as utilitarian as Ocado and losing the brand warmth that makes people evangelists.

design_directions.name: The Digital Market
design_directions.summary: Bet that GreenBasket wins on the one thing no competitor has — the feeling of a curated market with people and stories behind the food. Lead the experience with seasonal editorial, producer narratives, and impact framed as part of the story.
design_directions.differentiator: Producer stories and seasonal curation live in the browse flow, not a hidden blog; every product connects to a shareable human story, turning word-of-mouth into a built-in feature.
hmws_addressed: How might we make browsing feel like discovering a market rather than scanning a list?
How might we help shoppers feel what their order achieved without asking them to interpret a score?
design_directions.tradeoff: Does little for the Sunday-night efficiency shopper in the short term, needs an ongoing content operation, and may lose time-pressed users before the discovery investment pays back.

design_directions.name: Set It and Trust It
design_directions.summary: Bet that the winning move is to take the weekly shop off the user's plate entirely — a standing order the system maintains and adjusts for season and stock, with delivery and impact communicated to you rather than checked by you.
design_directions.differentiator: The system does the recurring work, not the user: a managed basket that proposes changes, handles stock-outs by your pre-set rules, and reports back — the shopper approves rather than assembles.
hmws_addressed: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual order without hunting down each item?
How might we keep shoppers in control when something they wanted turns out to be unavailable?
How might we make a delivery's timing predictable enough to plan a household around?
How might we help shoppers feel what their order achieved without asking them to interpret a score?
design_directions.tradeoff: Demands high trust in GreenBasket's judgment from users who've been burned by silent substitutions, reduces hands-on control, and is irrelevant to shoppers who browse for enjoyment.
